Subject: QuantumStep renewal — fleet reslice & conservative top‑up options

Hi Lydia / Mike,

Thanks again for taking the renewal conversation offline last week. We pulled together a short set of options after looking at your last 90 days of production traffic. TL;DR: your steady state is holding, but a recurring mid‑month batch causes a predictable 28–36% uplift across 48 hours. That pattern is what drove the variance last quarter.

I attached the 30‑day utilization extract for the cluster (quantumstep-30d-util.csv) — highlights below:
- Avg GPU utilization: 62%
- 95th percentile burst: 91% (durations typically 3–6 hrs)
- Latency SLO impacts observed when burst >85% under current slot mix

Options we recommend (brief):
1) Conservative Top‑up (recommended for predictable performance): +8 reserved H100 equiv. Runbook: staggered onboarding across 4 weeks, monitor KV cache hit rate. Expected impact: reduces burst utilization to ~75% and keeps latency headroom. Estimated incremental monthly spend: $42,000.
2) Seasonal Burst Pool: +12 burst H100 (shared burst pool, no immediate reserved commitment). Runbook: auto‑attach during mid‑month window, scale down afterwards. Expected impact: eliminates short spikes; cost is usage‑based and only incurred during burst windows. Simpler to trial for one quarter.
3) Quantization + slot reprofile: no new GPUs — applies model/offline compile tweaks to reduce token cost and ~10–12% GPU-demand reduction. Good as parallel optimization but takes ~6 weeks to validate.

Next steps I suggest: pick 1 or 2 of the above, share preferred timing, and we’ll produce a MAP (mutual action plan) and SOW addendum. I’ve looped in Kim and Vivek for capacity/ops sizing.

Best,
Ben

Ben / team / Lydia — ran the numbers off the 30d extract. Quick summary and assumptions up front: we assume H100 equiv slot pricing at list and a 10% committed discount baseline; current fleet mix is 70% reserved, 30% burst.

Recommendation set (concise):
A) Conservative reserved top‑up (Operationally safest)
- Add: 8 H100 reserved slots
- Impact: median utilization drops to ~58%; 95th p drops to ~78%
- Cost: incremental committed delta ≈ $42k/mo (≈ $504k/yr), with 30‑day pro‑rata onboarding.
- Rollback: 6‑month minimum (contractual), after which we can reprofile or transition 50% to burst with 60‑day notice.

B) Trial burst pool + targeted reprofile (Lower commitment, faster runway)
- Add: 12 burst H100 (usage billed by GPU‑hour) + run a 6‑week quantization pilot across two heavy models
- Impact: removes immediate spike pain; expected monthly bill ≈ $18–26k depending on burst hours; pilot could shave 10–12% demand.
- Rollback: immediate — burst usage stops automatically; pilot has rollback scripts for model weights and inference flags.

Operational notes:
- Observability: we’ll provide per‑route token headroom dashboards for the campaign window and a canary run for the first week of any reserved onboarding.
- SLA: reserved top‑up retains existing 99.9% availability SLA; burst pool offers best‑effort with prioritized attach when capacity exists (we can add SLA credits for a modest fee).

Attachments: short cost table (I’ll add to the MAP). I’ll prepare a MAP PDF (MAP-quantumstep-20261119.pdf) with these two options and a suggested timeline. If you want, we can price an intermediate hybrid (4 reserved + 8 burst).
